Containers: the cells of uniforms, vests and backpacks
Not applied yet. Apply keeps it.
Cells per container kind: Auto from its load, or Fixed. Class rules always win.
If you close now, they are lost.
One near-square block, up to %1 columns: a load of 280 makes %2 cells, %3 across and %4 down.
One block %1 wide with as many cells as the load gives, no more: a load of 1000 is %2 cells.
Cells = the container's load divided by the load per cell (%1 units, %2 kg), rounded up; worn gear gets a fifth more. A vest carrying 120 gets %3 cells, a backpack carrying 280 gets %4.
An item's size follows what it is, not its weight: rifles 4×2 to 7×2, handguns 2×1, launchers 6×2, magazines 1×1 to 2×2, grenades, optics and small things 1×1, helmets 2×2.
Your own rules for a class (Items and Containers steps) and mods' own settings win over all of this.

Only consumables stack: bandages, vials, cannulas, seals, syringes 5 per tile; injectors, sprays, tourniquets 4; lozenges, IV lines 10 (cable ties, ear plugs 20); rations, splints, first aid kits 5; blood bags, IV bags and devices 1. In crates, vehicles and piles on the ground the stack multiplier (Looting and searching) makes every stack larger.
One block %1 cells wide, %2 to %3 rows high by load: a plain uniform is 6×2.
Magazine pouches like a real rig: a tall 1×2, then a square 2×2 and so on, as many as the load needs, at most %1.
